Q: How to have three HTML sliders, indicating percentage; when one slider moved, other sliders are moved proportionally so the total of sliders = 100% A:

If slider 0 is at a, slider 1 is at b, and slider 2 is at c, and the user moves slider 2 to c', you have a change of c'-c that must be compensated for by adding c-c' (note the opposite sign) to the other two sliders. If this is to be done in proportion to the existing values of those two sliders, then slider 0 receives a portion a/(a+b) of the change and slider 1 receives a portion b/(a+b) of the change.

Thus slider 0 changes from a to a + a/(a+b)•(c-c') and slider 1 changes from b to b + b/(a+b)•(c-c').

Note that if a+b is 0, which occurs only when a and b are both 0, then you have a division by 0. In that case, you might wish to change the two sliders equally, setting them both to (c-c')/2. (Alternately, you could remember the previous ratios between the sliders, before they were set to 0, and use that information to distribute the changes. That introduces additional complications.)

Q: How do you create a file format? A:

For tools, check out the Kaitai Struct project and tools, or similar projects.

From that page:

Kaitai Struct is a declarative language used to describe various binary data structures, laid out in files or in memory: i.e. binary file formats, network stream packet formats, etc.

The main idea is that a particular format is described in Kaitai Struct language (.ksy file) and then can be compiled with ksc into source files in one of the supported programming languages. These modules will include a generated code for a parser that can read the described data structure from a file or stream and give access to it in a nice, easy-to-comprehend API.
